note: These six scenes come from five real calls plus one seeded demo record, all of them in calls/ and events.jsonl. Every utterance is verbatim, and the one that was seeded rather than spoken says so. The naive column is the value the model extracted from the transcript. The validated column is computed by the real validators when this page loads, so it cannot drift away from the code.

partials: Yes, my policy number is C411.
Yes, my policy number is KD4-1188.
scenes.transcript: Yes, my policy number is KD4-1188.
scenes.why: The recognizer's first reading of this utterance was C411. Its final answer was KD4-1188, a real policy on file, belonging to someone else. Transcription had been biased toward the list of valid policy numbers, so the recognizer could revise a number it was unsure of onto one of them. The exact-match check then passed on a match that transcription had manufactured. A validator is handed a value and a database, and it cannot ask where the value came from. Reading the number back to the caller is what catches this.

scenes.caller: spelling a policy number letter by letter
scenes.why: Spelled-out alphanumerics are where speech recognition is weakest.

scenes.caller: reading the twin of another policy on file
partials: bravo x-ray seven, four four two zero
scenes.transcript: bravo x-ray seven, four four two zero
scenes.why: BX7-4420 and BX7-4402 are both real policies belonging to different people. The readback separates them audibly. 'Four four two zero' against 'four four zero two'. This is the one scene taken from a seeded demo record rather than a live call, so the utterance was written by seed_demo.py and never spoken. The two policy numbers are real.

scenes.caller: giving a name one letter from the policy holder
scenes.why: The holder is Denise Holloway. A name one letter away is usually a mishearing rather than a second person, so it is worth asking about. Accepting it and refusing it are both guesses.

scenes.caller: giving a date with no year
scenes.why: A date without a year is not a date yet. Filling in the current year would silently decide whether the claim falls inside the policy period.

scenes.transcript: Someone hit my car on purpose.
scenes.naive: Someone hit my car on purpose
scenes.why: Collision and vandalism are an accident-versus-deliberate distinction that changes how the claim is handled. Two categories match, so the agent asks.
